checklist.step: Pull the current NFIP-appointed producer roster
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the PDB Appointment Report and filter by company NAIC number with line of authority Property/Casualty.
Export every producer currently appointed to bind or service SFIP policies for the WYO program.
Cross-check the export against the producer list in the agency/producer management system and flag any producer present in only one source.
Hand the reconciled roster to Producer Compliance Manager to open the renewal cycle.
checklist.done: the reconciled NFIP-appointed producer roster from NIPR matches the agency/producer management system.

checklist.step: Build the license and CE renewal calendar for the cycle
actions: For each roster producer, pull license expiration date and required CE hours from the NIPR license record.
Enter expiration date, CE-hour requirement and resident state into the renewal log's License tab.
Flag non-resident licenses separately since CE reciprocity rules differ by state.
Sort the calendar by nearest expiration date to prioritize outreach.
checklist.done: every appointed producer has a logged expiration date, CE-hour requirement and state on the renewal calendar.

checklist.step: Configure tiered renewal reminders
actions: Set automated triggers in the renewal log at 90, 60, 30 and 15 days before each expiration date.
Route 90/60-day reminders to the producer and agency principal; route 30/15-day reminders additionally to Producer Compliance Manager.
Confirm each reminder shows outstanding CE hours pulled from the NIPR CE Compliance tab.
checklist.done: every producer on the calendar has active 90/60/30/15-day reminders showing outstanding CE hours.

checklist.step: Track CE completion evidence as it is submitted
actions: Collect CE completion certificates from producers or pull completed-hours confirmation from the NIPR CE Compliance tab.
Log hours completed, course provider and completion date against the producer's renewal row.
Compare cumulative hours to the state's required threshold and mark the row Complete once met.
File the certificate image into the producer's compliance folder.
checklist.done: each producer's logged CE hours reach the state threshold with a certificate on file, or the shortfall is flagged.

checklist.step: Confirm the state renewal was filed and reissued
actions: On or after the producer's filing date, re-query NIPR Producer Search for the updated license status and new expiration date.
Update the renewal log with the confirmed new expiration date.
If the renewal shows still pending past its due date, contact the producer/agency principal directly and log the follow-up date.
checklist.done: NIPR shows a current, updated license status and expiration date for every producer due in the cycle.

checklist.step: Verify the company appointment remains active after renewal
actions: Re-run the PDB Appointment Report for the renewed producer to confirm the WYO company appointment is still Active.
Where a state auto-terminated the appointment on license lapse, re-file the appointment through NIPR Appointment Renewal once the license is current.
Update the Status field to Active in the agency/producer management system.
checklist.done: the producer shows an Active license and an Active company appointment in NIPR.

checklist.step: Suspend binding authority the day a license or CE requirement lapses
actions: On the expiration or CE cure-period deadline with no confirmed renewal, set the producer to Suspended – Not Bindable in the agency/producer management system.
Notify the producer, agency principal and the Underwriting Platform team so no new NFIP business can be bound under that producer code.
Record the suspension date and reason on the renewal log row.
checklist.done: no lapsed producer retains bindable status in the agency/producer management system or the underwriting platform.

checklist.step: Log every lapse as a licensing exception
actions: Open an exception record with producer name, license number, state, lapse date and duration.
Search the Policy Administration Platform for SFIP business bound under that producer code between the lapse date and reinstatement.
Assign the exception to Producer Compliance Manager with a target cure date.
checklist.done: every lapse has an exception record with quantified NFIP exposure and an assigned cure date.

checklist.step: Track reinstatement and clear the suspension
actions: Confirm via NIPR that the license shows Active and any reinstatement fee/CE deficiency has cleared.
Reactivate the producer in the agency/producer management system and restore bindable status.
Close the exception record with reinstatement date and NIPR confirmation attached.
checklist.done: the producer is reinstated in NIPR and the agency system, and the exception record closes with evidence.

checklist.step: Escalate producers still lapsed past the state grace period
actions: Identify producers still lapsed beyond the state's grace/reinstatement window from the renewal log.
Escalate to Compliance Officer with a recommendation: continued suspension, appointment termination, or agency-level remediation.
Where terminated, submit NIPR Appointment Termination and notify the agency principal in writing.
checklist.done: no producer remains lapsed past the state grace period without a documented termination or extension decision.

checklist.step: Reconcile the renewal log to NIPR monthly
actions: Pull a fresh PDB Appointment Report on the first business day of each month.
Compare license status, expiration date and appointment status against the renewal log for every producer.
Correct any discrepancy and note the correction date and source.
checklist.done: the renewal log matches the NIPR extract for 100% of appointed producers each month.

checklist.step: Report renewal-cycle status to Market Conduct Compliance
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard: producers due in 90 days, open CE shortfalls, currently suspended producers.
Route the dashboard to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and Producer Compliance Manager.
Flag any state with an outsized lapse rate for root-cause review.
checklist.done: a current renewal-status dashboard is published and reviewed by Market Conduct Compliance each month.

checklist.step: Assemble the completed renewal package into the producer's file
actions: Assemble prior and new NIPR license confirmation, CE certificates and appointment confirmation.
File the package into the producer's folder in the compliance evidence repository under the current cycle.
Tag the file with the next cycle's expiration date so it surfaces on the next calendar build.
checklist.done: the producer's compliance file holds the complete renewal package, tagged with the next cycle date.

checklist.step: Sign off the closed renewal cycle
actions: Review the closed renewal log, confirming every row is Complete, Suspended-with-exception-closed, or Terminated.
Spot-check five renewal packages directly against NIPR before signing.
Sign and date the cycle close-out summary.
checklist.done: Producer Compliance Manager has signed a cycle close-out summary with zero unresolved rows.

checklist.step: Retain renewal-cycle evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the renewal log export, NIPR confirmations, CE certificates and exception records into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to license lapse or producer termination date, whichever is later.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by producer name, state and license number.
checklist.done: renewal-cycle evidence is filed with a 7-year retention label and is searchable by producer, state and license number.

testing.step: Build the population of licenses/CE due in the quarter
actions: Extract the PDB Appointment Report for all NFIP-appointed producers with a license or CE deadline in the test quarter.
Reconcile the extract count to the renewal log count and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign and date the reconciled population count in the workpaper before drawing the sample.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between NIPR and the renewal log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every producer to a renewal log row
actions: Match each population producer to a renewal log row by producer and state.
List unmatched producers and any row missing a completion or suspension status as automatic exceptions.
Total the exception count and carry it forward into the sample selection step.
testing.done: every population producer is matched to a renewal log row or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers showing any lapse in the log.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 on-time renewals from the remainder, minimum 20 rows.
Record the seed and population size in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every lapsed producer.

testing.step: Re-verify license and appointment status directly in NIPR
actions: Query NIPR Producer Search and PDB Appointment Report for each sampled producer as of the test date.
Compare NIPR's status and expiration date to the renewal log entry; any difference is an exception.
Screenshot the NIPR record into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled producer has an independent NIPR re-verification captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Recompute CE hour totals against the state requirement
actions: Sum the logged CE hours per sampled producer from the filed certificates.
Compare the sum to the state's published CE-hour requirement for the license type.
Flag any producer marked Complete without meeting the hour threshold.
testing.done: recomputed CE totals agree with the state requirement for every sampled row, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Trace NFIP business bound during any lapse window
actions: For every sampled producer with a logged lapse, search the Policy Administration Platform for SFIP business bound under that producer code during the lapse.
Quantify premium and policy count bound while unlicensed or CE-deficient.
Treat any business bound during a lapse as a compliance breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: bound-during-lapse business is quantified for every lapsed sampled producer, with breaches flagged separately.

testing.step: Test suspension and reinstatement timeliness
actions: For each sampled lapse, compare the actual expiration date to the date binding authority was suspended in the underwriting platform.
Compare the reinstatement date to the date NIPR showed the license Active.
Flag any suspension that lagged the lapse date, or reinstatement that preceded NIPR confirmation.
testing.done: suspension and reinstatement dates align to NIPR status changes for every sampled lapse, or the lag is logged.

testing.step: Check reminder and escalation configuration
actions: Confirm the 90/60/30/15-day reminder log exists for each sampled producer.
Confirm escalation to Compliance Officer occurred for producers lapsed beyond the state grace period.
Flag missing reminders or missed escalations.
testing.done: reminder and escalation evidence exists for every sampled producer, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with producer, state, what was missed and NFIP exposure.
Assign root cause (missed roster pull, reminder not configured, agency non-response) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry any open exception into next quarter's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Capture the screening trigger from HR or Licensing
actions: Receive the new-hire or role-change record from HR Specialist for any role coded as NFIP-facing (claims, underwriting, producer appointment, servicing).
For producers, cross-check the NIPR appointment request that triggered the screen.
Open a screening case in the compliance evidence repository with hire date, role and target activation date.
Confirm the case is opened before the individual's system access or appointment is activated.
checklist.done: a screening case exists for the hire with role, hire date and target activation date, opened before access is granted.

checklist.step: Order the background check
actions: Submit the individual's consent-signed background order to the background-check vendor via the Credit Bureau & Data Services portal, requesting a criminal-history and breach-of-trust/dishonesty offense search.
Confirm the individual signed the Fair Credit Reporting Act disclosure/consent form on file with HR.
Set a 5-business-day follow-up if the report has not returned.
checklist.done: a signed consent is on file and the background order is confirmed submitted to the vendor.

checklist.step: Review the returned report for 1033-triggering convictions
actions: Read the returned report for any felony conviction involving dishonesty, breach of trust, or a related offense.
Cross-reference any hit against 18 U.S.C. 1033(e)'s covered-offense categories with Regulatory Counsel.
Record the finding (Clear / Conviction Found) with the offense, date and jurisdiction on the screening case.
checklist.done: the screening case shows a documented Clear or Conviction Found finding with supporting detail.

checklist.step: Check self-disclosure and prior-waiver history
actions: Compare the individual's self-disclosed conviction history from the application/hire form against the background report.
Search the compliance evidence repository for any prior 1033 waiver already on file for the individual.
Log any discrepancy between self-disclosure and the vendor report as a separate integrity flag.
checklist.done: self-disclosure is reconciled to the vendor report and any prior waiver is located or confirmed absent.

checklist.step: Restrict NFIP duties pending disposition
actions: Where a conviction is found, instruct HR Specialist to hold activation of any NFIP-facing system access or producer appointment.
Set the individual's status to Restricted in the screening case until a waiver decision is reached.
Notify the hiring manager of the restriction and expected timeline.
checklist.done: no individual with an unresolved conviction finding holds active NFIP-facing access or appointment.

checklist.step: Prepare the 1033 consent/waiver application
actions: Determine the correct consenting authority (state insurance commissioner or other regulator with jurisdiction) for the offense and role.
Assemble the waiver application: offense detail, sentence/completion evidence, rehabilitation evidence, role description and company sponsorship letter.
Route the draft to Compliance Officer for review before submission.
checklist.done: a complete waiver application package is assembled and reviewed by Compliance Officer.

checklist.step: Submit the waiver application and track its status
actions: Submit the waiver application to the applicable state regulator through that state's prescribed channel.
Log the submission date, regulator contact and expected decision timeline on the screening case.
Follow up at 30-day intervals until a decision is received.
checklist.done: the waiver submission date and tracking status are logged and followed up at 30-day intervals.

checklist.step: Record the waiver decision and update duty restriction
actions: Upon regulator decision, file the consent/denial letter into the screening case.

If approved, instruct HR Specialist and Producer Licensing Coordinator to activate NFIP-facing access/appointment; if denied, keep the restriction permanent and initiate role reassignment or separation with HR.
Update the screening case status to Waiver Approved or Waiver Denied with the decision date.
checklist.done: the screening case reflects the regulator's decision with the letter attached and access status updated accordingly.

checklist.step: Clear individuals with no conviction finding
actions: For Clear findings, set the screening case status to Cleared.
Notify HR Specialist and, for producers, Producer Licensing Coordinator that NFIP-facing activation may proceed.
File the background report into the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every Clear finding is closed with activation notified and the report filed.

checklist.step: Log any exception where duties began before screening cleared
actions: Where an audit or manager report shows NFIP duties began before the screen cleared, open an exception with the activation date and screen-clear date.
Assign the exception to Compliance Officer with a root-cause request to HR/hiring manager.
Set a remediation date and confirm access was retroactively restricted if the finding was adverse.
checklist.done: every early-activation instance is logged as an exception with an assigned owner and remediation date.

checklist.step: Schedule periodic re-screening
actions: Set a re-screen reminder for every NFIP-facing individual at the company's defined interval (aligned to producer license renewal or a fixed 5-year cycle for employees).
Trigger the same background-order workflow at the re-screen date.
Log the re-screen outcome on the individual's existing screening case.
checklist.done: every NFIP-facing individual has a scheduled re-screen date and an updated case on completion.

checklist.step: Reconcile the screening log against HRIS and NIPR placements
actions: Monthly, pull all NFIP-facing role placements and producer appointments from HRIS and NIPR.
Match each placement to an open or closed screening case.
Escalate any unmatched placement to Compliance Officer the same day.
checklist.done: every NFIP-facing placement in the month has a matching screening case, with no unmatched placements outstanding.

checklist.step: Report screening and waiver status to Compliance leadership
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard: screens in progress, restricted individuals, pending waivers and re-screens due.
Route the dashboard to Compliance Officer and Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
Flag any restriction open longer than 45 days for direct follow-up.
checklist.done: a current screening dashboard is published monthly with aged restrictions flagged.

checklist.step: Compliance Officer sign-off on conviction and waiver cases
actions: Review every case with a Conviction Found finding for the period.
Confirm the waiver decision (or ongoing restriction) is properly documented and access status matches the decision.
Sign and date each case file.
checklist.done: every conviction-finding case for the period carries a dated Compliance Officer sign-off.

checklist.step: Retain screening evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the background report, screening decision, waiver application and any regulator letter into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label from termination or waiver expiry, whichever is later.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by individual name and role.
checklist.done: screening evidence is filed with a 7-year retention label and is searchable by individual and role.

testing.step: Build the population of NFIP-facing placements in the period
actions: Extract all new hires, transfers and producer appointments coded to an NFIP-facing role in the test period from HRIS and NIPR.
Reconcile the extract count to the screening-case log and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign and date the reconciled population count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between HRIS/NIPR and the screening log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every placement to a screening case
actions: Match each population placement to a screening case by individual name and hire/appointment date.
List unmatched placements and any case missing a disposition as automatic exceptions.
Total the exception count and carry it forward into the sample selection step.
testing.done: every population placement is matched to a screening case or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of cases with a Conviction Found finding or an open waiver.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 Clear cases from the remainder.
Record the seed and population size in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every conviction/waiver case.

testing.step: Re-perform the conviction review on the sample
actions: Re-read the underlying background report for each sampled case without looking at the recorded finding first.
Reach an independent Clear/Conviction conclusion and compare to the logged finding.
Log any difference as an exception, including a missed conviction.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent re-performance note and any difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify activation timing against screening clearance
actions: Pull the system-access or appointment activation date from HRIS/NIPR for each sampled individual.
Compare it to the screening case's Cleared or Waiver Approved date.
Any activation before clearance is a compliance breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled individual was activated before screening clearance, or the breach is separately reported.

testing.step: Test waiver application completeness and timeliness
actions: For each sampled waiver case, confirm the application package included offense detail, rehabilitation evidence and sponsorship letter.
Confirm the submission date preceded the individual's NFIP engagement.
Confirm the final consent/denial letter is on file and matches the access decision made.
testing.done: every sampled waiver case has a complete, timely application and a matching, filed regulator decision.

testing.step: Check re-screen scheduling and completion
actions: For individuals due a re-screen in the period, confirm a re-screen record exists and the outcome is logged.
Flag any individual past their re-screen due date with no record.
Compare the re-screen due date logged to the individual's original hire or last-screen date to confirm the interval was correctly applied.
testing.done: every individual due a re-screen has a logged outcome, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Confirm retention labeling on sampled case files
actions: Open each sampled case in the compliance evidence repository and confirm the 7-year retention label is applied.
Confirm the file is retrievable by individual name.
Confirm the retention start date matches the later of termination or waiver expiry as recorded on the case.
testing.done: every sampled case carries the correct retention label and is retrievable by name.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with individual, role, what was missed and NFIP exposure.
Assign root cause (screen not ordered, early activation, incomplete waiver package) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry any open exception into next quarter's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and any breaches called out separately.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Extract the internal active-producer roster
actions: Export every producer coded Active with NFIP/flood line-of-business authority from the agency/producer management system.
Include producer name, NPN (National Producer Number), resident state, appointed states and status.
Save the export with a quarter-end timestamp into the reconciliation workpaper.
checklist.done: the internal active-producer roster is exported with NPN and appointed states for the quarter-end date.

checklist.step: Extract the NIPR PDB appointment records
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the PDB Appointment Report and filter by company NAIC number for the same quarter-end date.
Export appointment status, effective date and state for every producer appointed to the company.
Save the export alongside the internal roster in the reconciliation workpaper.
checklist.done: the NIPR PDB appointment export for the same quarter-end date is saved in the workpaper.

checklist.step: Match the two extracts by NPN and state
actions: Join the internal roster and NIPR extract on NPN plus appointed state.
Flag rows present internally but missing from NIPR (unappointed-but-active), and rows present in NIPR but missing internally (appointed-but-unrecorded).
Flag status mismatches where one source shows Active and the other shows Terminated or Lapsed.
checklist.done: a matched dataset exists with every discrepancy category flagged by NPN and state.

checklist.step: Investigate each unappointed-but-active discrepancy
actions: For each producer active internally without a matching NIPR appointment, check whether an appointment request was ever filed.
If none was filed, submit the NIPR Appointment Request immediately for the state(s) in question.
Suspend the producer's binding authority for that state in the agency/producer management system until the appointment confirms.
checklist.done: every unappointed-but-active producer has a filed NIPR appointment request and suspended binding authority until confirmed.

checklist.step: Investigate each appointed-but-unrecorded discrepancy
actions: For each NIPR appointment with no matching internal roster row, determine whether the producer should still be active.
If active, add the missing row to the agency/producer management system with correct status and states.
If the producer left the agency or was terminated, file NIPR Appointment Termination for that state.
checklist.done: every appointed-but-unrecorded producer is either added to the internal roster or terminated in NIPR.

checklist.step: Resolve status mismatches
actions: For each status mismatch, pull the underlying event (termination notice, license lapse, appointment renewal) that explains the difference.
Correct the lagging system to match the authoritative event date.
Note the correction, source event and date on the discrepancy log row.
checklist.done: every status mismatch is resolved to a single, source-supported status in both systems.

checklist.step: Quantify NFIP business exposure behind unresolved discrepancies
actions: For any discrepancy that implies a period of unappointed binding, search the Policy Administration Platform for SFIP business bound under that producer code during the gap.
Record policy count and premium bound during the unappointed period.
Route any nonzero exposure to Producer Compliance Manager for review.
checklist.done: exposure is quantified for every discrepancy that implied an unappointed binding period.

checklist.step: Log every discrepancy in the reconciliation report
actions: Enter each discrepancy as a row: producer, NPN, state, discrepancy type, resolution action, resolution date, exposure quantified.
Attach the reconciliation report to the quarter's compliance evidence folder.
Set status Open until every row is resolved.
checklist.done: the reconciliation report lists every discrepancy with a resolution and a resolution date.

checklist.step: Escalate discrepancies with exposure or unresolved past 10 business days
actions: Review any discrepancy with nonzero NFIP exposure or open past the 10-business-day close target.
Escalate to Compliance Officer with the exposure amount and proposed remediation.
Document the decision and revised close date on the discrepancy row.
checklist.done: every discrepancy with exposure or aged past 10 business days has a documented escalation decision.

checklist.step: Confirm the corrected rosters agree post-resolution
actions: Re-pull both the internal roster and the NIPR PDB extract after all corrections are made.
Re-run the match and confirm zero unresolved discrepancies remain.
Save the post-correction match as the final reconciliation record.
checklist.done: a post-correction match shows zero unresolved discrepancies between the two rosters.

checklist.step: Report the quarter's reconciliation results
actions: Publish the discrepancy count, categories and resolution timeliness for the quarter.
Route the report to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and Producer Compliance Manager.
Trend discrepancy rate quarter over quarter to spot process drift.
checklist.done: the quarter's reconciliation results and trend are published and reviewed by Market Conduct Compliance.

checklist.step: Update procedure or NIPR feed configuration on recurring root causes
actions: Where the same discrepancy type recurs across quarters, identify the process gap (e.g., appointment requests not filed at onboarding).
Propose a procedure or system fix to Producer Compliance Manager.
Document the fix and its effective quarter in the procedure document.
checklist.done: recurring discrepancy root causes have a documented process or system fix with an effective date.

checklist.step: Sign off the closed quarter reconciliation
actions: Review the final reconciliation record and discrepancy log for the quarter.
Confirm every discrepancy row shows a resolution date and, where applicable, an escalation outcome.
Sign and date the quarter close-out.
checklist.done: Producer Compliance Manager has signed the quarter's reconciliation close-out with zero open rows.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation package into the compliance evidence repository
actions: Move the internal roster export, NIPR extract, discrepancy log and sign-off into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the reconciliation date.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by quarter and producer NPN.
checklist.done: the reconciliation package is filed with a 7-year retention label, searchable by quarter and NPN.

checklist.step: Retain trend data for the exam-readiness file
actions: Add the quarter's discrepancy count and resolution time to the rolling trend log.
Copy the trend log and current reconciliation report into the market-conduct exam readiness file.
Confirm the exam readiness file reflects the most recently closed quarter within 5 business days of sign-off.
checklist.done: the exam readiness file holds the current quarter's reconciliation report and an up-to-date trend log.

testing.step: Build the population for the sampled quarter
actions: Independently re-extract the internal active-producer roster and the NIPR PDB appointment records as of the sampled quarter-end date.
Reconcile the row counts to the retained reconciliation workpaper for that quarter.
Sign and date the reconciled population count before proceeding to the match.
testing.done: the independently re-extracted population is reconciled in count to the retained workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the match independently
actions: Join the re-extracted internal roster and NIPR extract on NPN and state.
Independently identify unappointed-but-active, appointed-but-unrecorded and status-mismatch rows.
Compare the independently identified discrepancies to the discrepancies logged for that quarter.
testing.done: an independently re-performed match exists and is compared line-for-line to the logged discrepancies.

testing.step: Select the sample of discrepancies to trace
actions: Take 100% of discrepancies that carried nonzero NFIP exposure.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 of the remaining resolved discrepancies.
Record the seed and total discrepancy count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every discrepancy with quantified exposure.

testing.step: Trace each sampled discrepancy's resolution to source evidence
actions: For each sampled discrepancy, re-query NIPR (and the agency/producer management system) for the current status.
Confirm the resolution recorded matches the authoritative source event (termination notice, appointment filing, license update).
Flag any resolution not supported by a dated source document.
testing.done: every sampled discrepancy's resolution is traced to a dated source document, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Recompute exposure on discrepancies with a bound-business gap
actions: For each sampled exposure discrepancy, independently search the Policy Administration Platform for business bound during the unappointed gap.
Compare the independently computed policy count and premium to the figure logged in the reconciliation report.
Log any variance between the independent and logged figures with its dollar magnitude.
testing.done: recomputed exposure matches the logged figure for every sampled discrepancy, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test timeliness of the quarter's close
actions: Confirm the reconciliation report date and the Producer Compliance Manager sign-off date fall within 10 business days of quarter-end.
Flag any quarter that closed late and note the delay length.
Record the actual close-day count in the workpaper for trend comparison against prior quarters.
testing.done: the sampled quarter's close timing is verified against the 10-business-day target.

testing.step: Verify escalations were raised for qualifying discrepancies
actions: Confirm every discrepancy with exposure, or aged past 10 business days, has a logged Compliance Officer escalation.
Flag any qualifying discrepancy without an escalation record.
Confirm the escalation record names a proposed remediation and a revised close date.
testing.done: every qualifying discrepancy in the sample has a logged escalation, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Confirm retention and searchability of the reconciliation package
actions: Retrieve the sampled quarter's reconciliation package from the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm the 7-year retention label is applied and the package is searchable by quarter and NPN.
Confirm the package includes the internal roster export, NIPR extract, discrepancy log and sign-off together.
testing.done: the sampled quarter's package is retrievable with the correct retention label applied.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with producer, state, discrepancy type and NFIP exposure.
Assign root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry any open exception into next quarter's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Maintain the master inventory of required NFIP conduct-area procedures
actions: In the GRC platform's policy module, maintain one inventory row per conduct area: claims adjustment, producer licensing, accounting segregation, complaint handling, MCAS reporting.
For each row record the current procedure version, owner, last review date and next review-due date.
Add a new inventory row whenever a WYO Arrangement amendment or FEMA bulletin creates a new conduct obligation.
checklist.done: the GRC inventory has one current row per required conduct area with owner and review-due date.

checklist.step: Monitor FEMA/Bureau and NFIP source material for procedure-triggering changes
actions: Subscribe to FEMA NFIP Bureau and WYO bulletins and monitor NFIP Claims Manual and WYO Accounting Procedures Manual updates.
Log each new bulletin/manual release with its effective date and the conduct area(s) it touches.
Route affected-conduct-area findings to the relevant procedure owner within 5 business days of the source release.
checklist.done: every new bulletin or manual update is logged and routed to the affected procedure owner within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Draft or update the procedure for claims adjustment standards
actions: Compare the current claims adjustment procedure against the latest NFIP Claims Manual and any claims guidance bulletins.
Redline changes needed to keep adjustment standards, documentation requirements and reinspection cooperation steps current.
Route the redline to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for review.
checklist.done: the claims adjustment procedure redline reflects the current NFIP Claims Manual and is routed for review.

checklist.step: Draft or update the procedure for producer licensing
actions: Compare the current licensing procedure against 44 CFR Part 61 Appendix A(1) and any state licensing-rule changes.
Confirm the procedure cross-references the license/CE renewal tracking and roster reconciliation procedures.
Route the redline to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for review.
checklist.done: the producer licensing procedure redline is current and cross-referenced, and routed for review.

checklist.step: Draft or update the accounting/ledger segregation procedure
actions: Compare the current procedure against the WYO Accounting Procedures Manual Chapter on the Financial Control Plan.
Confirm the procedure specifies the dedicated NFIP flood GL segment/cost center codes that keep flood premium, loss, expense and recoverable balances separate from company-risk business.
Route the redline to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for review.
checklist.done: the accounting segregation procedure redline names the current NFIP GL segment codes and is routed for review.

checklist.step: Draft or update the complaint-handling procedure
actions: Compare the current complaint procedure against NAIC Market Regulation Handbook complaint-handling standards and state DOI complaint-response timelines.
Confirm intake, categorization, response-time and escalation steps are current.
Route the redline to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for review.
checklist.done: the complaint-handling procedure redline reflects current response-time standards and is routed for review.

checklist.step: Draft or update the MCAS/regulatory reporting procedure
actions: Compare the current reporting procedure against the NAIC's current MCAS data-call specification and filing deadline.
Confirm the procedure names the current filing system, data-extract source and sign-off chain.
Route the redline to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for review.
checklist.done: the MCAS reporting procedure redline reflects the current data-call specification and is routed for review.

checklist.step: Run a gap analysis across the full procedure set
actions: Compare each conduct area's procedure scope against the current WYO Arrangement text and supporting citations.
Identify any obligation with no corresponding procedure step and any procedure step with no current obligation.
Document findings and required fixes in the gap-analysis workpaper.
checklist.done: a gap-analysis workpaper exists mapping every obligation to a procedure step, with any gaps documented.

checklist.step: Route each redlined procedure for legal review
actions: Review each redline for consistency with the WYO Financial Assistance/Subsidy Arrangement and applicable federal/state law.
Flag any redline that creates a legal exposure or conflicts with another procedure.
Return comments to the drafting owner or clear the redline for final approval.
checklist.done: every redline has a documented legal review outcome before it proceeds to approval.

checklist.step: Approve and version the updated procedure
actions: Review the final redline and legal comments and approve or reject.
Publish the approved procedure as a new version in SharePoint with a version number, effective date and superseded-version link.
Update the GRC inventory row with the new version number and next review-due date.
checklist.done: the approved procedure is published as a new numbered version with the GRC inventory updated.

checklist.step: Communicate and train on the updated procedure
actions: Notify all roles named in the procedure of the update, its effective date and what changed.
Schedule refresher training where the change affects day-to-day steps (e.g., a new claims documentation field).
Log training completion by role in the learning management system.
checklist.done: affected roles are notified, trained where needed, and completion is logged.

checklist.step: Track and close overdue-review exceptions
actions: Pull the GRC inventory for any procedure past its review-due date.
Open an exception with procedure name, owner, days overdue and cause.
Close the exception once the review completes and the new version is published.
checklist.done: every overdue procedure has an exception opened and closed with a published new version.

checklist.step: Reconcile the procedure inventory to the current citation set
actions: Re-read the current supporting citations (44 CFR 62.23 series, NFIP Claims Manual, WYO Accounting Procedures Manual) against the GRC inventory.
Confirm no citation has changed without a corresponding procedure update.
Sign the citation-reconciliation note in the gap-analysis workpaper.
checklist.done: the citation set is reconciled to the procedure inventory with a signed reconciliation note.

checklist.step: Present the annual procedure-governance summary to Compliance leadership
actions: Summarize the year's reviews, redlines, gaps closed and outstanding exceptions.
Present to the Compliance Committee with the current GRC inventory extract attached.
Record any Committee-directed action with an owner and due date.
checklist.done: the annual summary is presented to the Compliance Committee with actions recorded.

checklist.step: Retain procedure versions and governance evidence
actions: Move every superseded procedure version, approval record and gap-analysis workpaper into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the version's supersede date.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by conduct area and version number.
checklist.done: procedure versions and governance evidence are filed with a 7-year retention label, searchable by conduct area.

testing.step: Build the population of required procedures
actions: Extract the full GRC procedure inventory for the NFIP program with owner, version and review-due date.
Independently list every conduct area implied by the WYO Arrangement citations and compare to the inventory for coverage gaps.
Sign and date the reconciled population count before proceeding to sampling.
testing.done: the procedure population is extracted and independently checked for conduct-area coverage.

testing.step: Reconcile inventory rows to review-due status
actions: For every inventory row, compute days since last review and compare to the annual review requirement.
List any row past due, and any conduct area with no procedure at all, as automatic exceptions.
Total the exception count and carry it forward into the sample selection step.
testing.done: every inventory row's review status is computed and exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Select the sample of procedures to test
actions: Take 100% of procedures flagged overdue or missing.
Take a random sample of 5 current procedures from the remainder.
Record the selection method and population size in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every overdue or missing procedure.

testing.step: Re-read each sampled procedure against its source citation
actions: Pull the current text of each sampled procedure's underlying citation (44 CFR section, Claims Manual chapter, Accounting Procedures Manual chapter).
Compare the procedure's steps to the current citation text without relying on the prior gap analysis.
Log any mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled procedure has an independent citation comparison with any mismatch logged.

testing.step: Verify approval and version-control evidence
actions: Open each sampled procedure in SharePoint and confirm a version number, effective date and Compliance Officer approval signature exist.
Confirm the prior version is retained and linked as superseded.
Flag any procedure missing an approval signature or version link.
testing.done: every sampled procedure has verified approval and version-control evidence, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Verify legal review occurred before approval
actions: Confirm a General Counsel review comment or clearance exists for each sampled procedure's most recent redline.
Flag any procedure approved without a documented legal review.
Confirm the review comment date precedes the Compliance Officer's final approval date.
testing.done: legal review evidence is confirmed for every sampled procedure, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Test training completion tied to the sampled procedures
actions: For sampled procedures that changed a role's day-to-day steps, pull the training completion log for affected roles.
Confirm completion dates fall on or after the procedure's effective date.
Flag any affected role with no completion record.
testing.done: training completion is confirmed for affected roles on sampled procedures, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Trace overdue-procedure exceptions to closure
actions: For every sampled overdue procedure, confirm an exception was opened, has an owner and a remediation date.
Confirm closure evidence (new published version) exists where the exception shows closed.
Confirm the new published version's effective date falls after the exception's remediation date.
testing.done: every sampled overdue procedure has a traceable exception with owner, remediation date and closure evidence where applicable.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with procedure name, conduct area, what was missed and impact.
Assign root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry any open exception into next year's mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Pull the current-year NAIC MCAS data-call specification
actions: Log in to the NAIC gateway and open the current reporting year's MCAS Data Call specification for the relevant line(s).
Note every data element, interrogatory and the participating-state list for the year.
Diff the specification against last year's version and flag any new or changed element.
checklist.done: the current-year specification is pulled with new/changed elements flagged against the prior year.

checklist.step: Map each MCAS data element to its source system field
actions: For each required element, identify the source system (Claims Platform, Policy Administration Platform) and the exact field or calculated measure.
Update the data-element mapping document for any specification change identified in the prior step.
Route new or changed mappings to the source-system data owner for confirmation.
checklist.done: every MCAS data element has a confirmed source-system mapping for the current year.

checklist.step: Extract the source data for the reporting period
actions: Run the extraction query against the data warehouse for the full reporting period, by state and line of business.
Reconcile record counts (claims closed, policies in force, complaints received) to the source system's own period-end totals.
Resolve any count difference before proceeding to build the filing.
checklist.done: the source extract is reconciled to source-system period-end totals for every state.

checklist.step: Run NAIC edit checks against the built data set
actions: Load the built data set into the MCAS filing application's validation/edit-check function.
Review every edit-check warning or error and research the cause in the source data.
Correct the source mapping or extract logic and re-run the edit checks until clean.
checklist.done: the data set passes the NAIC edit checks with zero unresolved errors.

checklist.step: Draft the narrative interrogatory responses
actions: For each narrative interrogatory in the data call, draft a response grounded in the current reporting year's operational facts.
Cross-check narrative responses against the numeric data elements for internal consistency.
Route the draft to Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for content review.
checklist.done: narrative interrogatory responses are drafted, internally consistent, and routed for content review.

checklist.step: Review the built filing for content accuracy
actions: Review the numeric data elements and narrative responses against known operational events for the year (exam findings, complaint trends, claims backlogs).
Flag any figure inconsistent with known events for Regulatory Reporting Analyst to re-verify.
Confirm the state list matches the company's actual participating-state footprint.
checklist.done: content review is complete with any flagged inconsistency re-verified and resolved.

checklist.step: Obtain sign-off from Regulatory Reporting Manager
actions: Review the final data set, edit-check results and narrative responses.
Confirm the filing package is complete for every participating state.
Sign and date the pre-submission approval.
checklist.done: Regulatory Reporting Manager has signed the pre-submission approval for the complete filing package.

checklist.step: Submit the MCAS filing in the NAIC application
actions: In the NAIC MCAS filing application, upload the final validated data set and narrative responses per state.
Submit before the April 30 due date (or the state-specific due date if earlier).
Capture the submission confirmation number and timestamp for each state submitted.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted for every participating state before its due date with a captured confirmation number.

checklist.step: Verify submission acceptance
actions: Re-open the MCAS filing application and confirm each state's submission status shows Accepted (not Pending or Rejected).
For any Rejected status, research the rejection reason and correct and resubmit before the due date.
Log the final accepted status and date for every state.
checklist.done: every participating state's submission shows Accepted status with the confirming date logged.

checklist.step: Log any late or rejected filing as an exception
actions: Open an exception for any state not submitted by its due date, or any rejection not cleared before the due date.
Record root cause, days late and the corrected submission date.
Assign the exception to Regulatory Reporting Manager for sign-off on the corrective filing.
checklist.done: every late or rejected filing has an exception with root cause and a corrected submission date.

checklist.step: Track and process any post-filing amendment
actions: Where a data or narrative error is found after submission, prepare the amended data set and change summary.
Route the amendment through the same content review and Regulatory Reporting Manager sign-off before resubmission.
Log the amendment reason, original and corrected values, and resubmission date.
checklist.done: any post-filing amendment is re-reviewed, signed off and logged with the original and corrected values.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filed data set to the general ledger and claims system
actions: Compare the MCAS-reported claim counts and premium figures to the period-end general ledger and Claims Platform totals.
Document and resolve any variance before closing the filing cycle.
File the reconciliation as part of the filing evidence package.
checklist.done: the filed data set is reconciled to the general ledger and Claims Platform with variances resolved.

checklist.step: Report the filing cycle outcome to Compliance leadership
actions: Summarize submission timeliness, edit-check results and any exceptions for the year.
Present the summary to the Compliance Committee.
Record any Committee-directed action for next year's cycle.
checklist.done: the filing cycle outcome is presented to the Compliance Committee with any directed action recorded.

checklist.step: Retain the MCAS filing evidence package
actions: Move the source extract, edit-check log, narrative responses, sign-offs and submission confirmations into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the filing date.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by reporting year and state.
checklist.done: the MCAS filing package is filed with a 7-year retention label, searchable by year and state.

checklist.step: Update the data-element mapping for next year's cycle
actions: Note any specification, source-system or organizational change encountered during the year that will affect next year's mapping.
Update the mapping document proactively ahead of the next data-call release.
Confirm the updated mapping with the source-system data owner.
checklist.done: the mapping document is updated for known changes ahead of next year's data-call kickoff.

testing.step: Build the population of the filed MCAS data set
actions: Pull the final submitted data set and confirmation record for every participating state from the NAIC MCAS filing application.
Reconcile the submitted record counts to the retained source extract for the reporting year.
Sign and date the reconciled population count before proceeding to sampling.
testing.done: the filed population is reconciled to the retained source extract for every state.

testing.step: Reconcile submission dates to due dates per state
actions: For every participating state, compare the confirmed submission date/time to that state's MCAS due date.
List any state submitted late, or any state with no confirmed Accepted status, as an automatic exception.
Record the days-late count for each late state in the workpaper.
testing.done: every state's submission timeliness is checked and late/missing submissions are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Select the sample of data elements to re-derive
actions: Take 100% of narrative interrogatory responses.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 numeric data elements spread across states.
Record the seed and total element count in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every narrative response.

testing.step: Independently re-derive the sampled numeric elements from source systems
actions: Re-run the source query for each sampled data element directly against the Claims Platform / Policy Administration Platform, independent of the analyst's saved extract.
Compare the independently derived value to the filed value.
Log any variance as an exception with the magnitude and direction.
testing.done: each sampled numeric element has an independent re-derivation compared to the filed value.

testing.step: Test the narrative interrogatory responses for factual support
actions: For each narrative response, identify the underlying operational fact or record it describes.
Trace that fact to a source document (exam report, complaint log, claims backlog report).
Flag any narrative response with no traceable support.
testing.done: every narrative response is traced to a supporting source document, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Recompute the reconciliation to the general ledger and Claims Platform
actions: Independently pull period-end claim counts and premium totals from the general ledger and Claims Platform.
Compare to the filed MCAS totals and to the reconciliation retained by Regulatory Reporting.
Flag any unresolved variance.
testing.done: the general ledger/Claims Platform reconciliation is independently recomputed and compared to the retained reconciliation.

testing.step: Verify edit-check clearance evidence
actions: Retrieve the edit-check log from the NAIC MCAS filing application for the sampled reporting year.
Confirm every warning/error shown was researched and cleared before the final submission.
Flag any unresolved edit-check item present in the final filed data.
testing.done: edit-check clearance is confirmed for the sampled year, or unresolved items are flagged.

testing.step: Verify sign-off evidence
actions: Confirm the Regulatory Reporting Manager pre-submission approval is dated before the submission timestamp for each state.
Flag any state submitted without a preceding sign-off.
Confirm the sign-off references the same final data set version that was actually submitted.
testing.done: pre-submission sign-off is confirmed to precede submission for every state, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with state, data element, what was missed and impact.
Assign root cause (source mapping error, late extraction, missed due date) and an owner.

testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where needed, an amendment plan.

checklist.step: Investigate the root cause of each flagged breach

checklist.done: every systemic breach has an approved remediation plan tracked in the GRC platform.

Confirm every action tied to the finding shows Verified status.
Route the package to Compliance Manager for closure sign-off.
checklist.done: a complete closure package with verified evidence for every action is routed for sign-off.

checklist.step: Get Compliance Manager sign-off and notify the regulator of closure
actions: Review the closure package and sign off that the finding is fully remediated.
Where the regulator requires closure notification, send the closure letter (cleared by General Counsel) confirming completion.
Log the regulator's closure acknowledgment, if any, on the finding record.
checklist.done: Compliance Manager has signed off closure and, where required, the regulator's closure acknowledgment is logged.

checklist.step: Feed systemic root causes back into procedure governance
actions: For any finding whose root cause was a procedure gap, notify the procedure owner to trigger an out-of-cycle procedure update.
Confirm the update is reflected in the GRC procedure inventory and the exam readiness binder.
Close the loop by noting the procedure version that incorporated the fix on the finding record.
checklist.done: every procedure-gap root cause results in a logged procedure update referenced on the finding record.

checklist.step: Retain the full finding-to-closure evidence trail
actions: Move the exam report/reinspection letter, CAP, execution tickets, verification results and closure correspondence into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the closure date.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by finding number and exam/reinspection date.
checklist.done: the full finding-to-closure trail is filed with a 7-year retention label, searchable by finding number and exam date.

testing.step: Build the population of findings opened or closed in the period
actions: Extract every finding record from AuditBoard opened or closed in the test quarter.
Reconcile the extract count to the source exam reports/reinspection letters for the period.
Sign and date the reconciled population count before proceeding to sampling.
testing.done: the finding population is reconciled to the source exam reports and reinspection letters.

testing.step: Reconcile each finding to a CAP with a due date
actions: Match each population finding to a CAP record with an owner and due date.
List any finding with no CAP, no owner, or no due date as an automatic exception.
Total the exception count and carry it forward into the sample selection step.
testing.done: every population finding is matched to a complete CAP record or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of findings closed late or still open past their due date.
Take a seeded random sample of 10 on-time-closed findings from the remainder.
Record the seed and population size in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every late or overdue finding.

testing.step: Re-perform the verification test behind each sampled closed finding
actions: Independently re-test whether the corrective action actually resolved the cited deficiency (re-sample the same file type, re-check the same procedure or system control).
Compare the independent result to the verification result recorded when the finding was closed.
Log any difference as an exception, including a finding closed without the deficiency actually fixed.
testing.done: each sampled closed finding has an independent re-verification compared to the recorded result.

testing.step: Recompute due-date and closure-timeliness math
actions: For each sampled finding, recompute the CAP due date from the exam report/reinspection letter's stated timeline (or the 90-day default).
Compare the recomputed due date and the actual closure date.
Treat any late closure with no written extension as a compliance breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: due-date math is recomputed for every sampled finding, with unextended late closures reported as breaches.

testing.step: Trace escalation evidence for at-risk findings
actions: For sampled findings that tracked behind schedule, confirm a T-15-day escalation to Compliance Officer exists.
Confirm any extension request was submitted in writing before the original due date.
Flag any at-risk finding with no escalation record.
testing.done: escalation and extension evidence is confirmed for every sampled at-risk finding, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Verify legal clearance and regulator correspondence
actions: Confirm each sampled CAP carries a General Counsel clearance predating its submission.
Confirm the regulator's acknowledgment (of the CAP and, where required, of closure) is on file.
Flag any sampled finding missing legal clearance or regulator correspondence.
testing.done: legal clearance and regulator correspondence are confirmed for every sampled finding, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Check systemic findings fed back into procedure governance
actions: For sampled findings with a procedure-gap root cause, confirm the referenced procedure version was actually updated in the GRC procedure inventory.
Flag any procedure-gap finding with no corresponding procedure update.
Confirm the procedure's new effective date falls after the finding's closure date.
testing.done: procedure updates are confirmed for every sampled procedure-gap finding, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with finding number, what was missed and regulatory impact.
Assign root cause (weak verification, missed escalation, no legal clearance) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any breach, open a self-report assessment with General Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where needed, a self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and any breaches called out separately.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is filed and reported to the Compliance Committee.
